reference_findings.diagnosis: Possible vasospastic angina; diagnosis requires appropriate clinical context and, when indicated, specialist testing. A normal angiogram does not exclude vasomotor disease.
reference_findings.risk_assessment: Variable / mechanism-focused; qualitative simulation label only, not a validated score.

investigation_reports.ecg: Resting ECG normal between episodes; one fictional captured symptomatic ECG shows transient ischemic ST shift.
investigation_reports.laboratory_panel: Serial hs-cTn remains below fictional threshold without rise/fall in this episode; electrolytes and renal function available.
investigation_reports.echocardiography: LVEF 60%; no regional wall-motion abnormality at rest.
investigation_reports.coronary_or_other_imaging: Reference angiography: no obstructive stenosis; TIMI 3 flow. Vasoreactivity testing is not included in the initial report and must only be represented as an expert-led diagnostic option in the simulator.
investigation_reports.initial_vitals: HR 72 bpm; BP 124/76 mmHg; RR 15/min; SpO2 99%; asymptomatic at the current snapshot.
investigation_reports.not_supplied: Any test not explicitly listed is not ordered/not available; it must not be interpreted as normal.

history.chief_complaint: Brief episodes of chest tightness at rest, often overnight, resolving spontaneously.
history.history_of_present_illness: Episodes are intermittent; exertional tolerance between episodes is relatively preserved. Symptoms alone are not diagnostic.
medication_reconciliation: Medication list to be reconciled; substances that may affect vasomotor tone should be documented by clinical reviewer

differential_diagnosis: Panic/anxiety-related symptoms only after appropriate evaluation

pathway_review.label: Consider specialist evaluation for ANOCA/INOCA endotypes
pathway_review.reason: Testing choice depends on symptom pattern, local expertise, contraindications and clinical review.

pathway_review.label: Dismiss symptoms because no obstructive lesion is seen
pathway_review.reason: Non-obstructive anatomy does not exclude vasomotor or microvascular causes.

pathway_review.label: Diagnose vasospasm from symptom timing alone
pathway_review.reason: Timing can be a clue but is not sufficient proof.

reference_findings.safety_review: Any provocation-testing depiction must remain high-level and clinician-supervised; include informed consent, rhythm monitoring and contraindication review in the educational checklist, not operational dosing or administration steps.
reference_findings.simulated_clinical_course: Reference branch: further specialist functional assessment is selected; case debrief explains uncertainty and distinguishes epicardial from microvascular endotypes.
learning_objectives: Avoid premature dismissal or diagnosis from one clue.
Understand that specialized testing requires expertise.
reference_findings.review_note: Synthetic scenario. Clinical values and pathway labels require qualified interventional cardiology review before deployment. Educational use only; not real-patient guidance.
